lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Edric's so hot now.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: As you come into the room, you find it quite large and a little bit oddly shaped. It's about 30 feet wide, 30 feet deep, and 30 feet tall. First, it's just sort of a scene of destruction: tables and chairs have been smashed and overturned. There's a sort of counter by the door—we're just going to assume that Comprehend Languages is up as a ritual indefinitely, for the sake of simplicity—that at one point read “Current Occupants” and would have had a number below it, but has been smashed apart. There's a giant tapestry on one side that's been pulled down and mangled. On the far wall across from the door, so 30 feet in front of you, almost the entire space is taken up with massive pipes and tubes and turbines, stuff made of cast copper and iron that's almost—I don't know—steam-pump-looking. There's a hum that comes from all of it, but no obviously moving parts. The door you just walked through is in the center of one wall. There's a door in the center of the left wall, a door in the center of the right wall, and a spiral staircase in the center of the room that goes up and down. You're muted, Eric.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Thanks. The occupancy sign—what was the story with that? It would have listed the number of people in the room? Oh, no, the maximum number of people?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, no. It looked like it had those little flippy numbers like the clocks did. So perhaps it might have been a—your guess is that it was a running tally of occupants.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: That's weird.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: And presumably we try opening the door we just came in, and—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh yeah, it just opens right back out again.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Oh, okay. Well, if we're trying to get to room number 27, and we have four not-necessarily-numbered options for leaving this room, the second room that we enter won't necessarily be the 27th room by any math. You know, if it's random, one-fourth of all the options in the room that we start off in. So I don't exactly know how to get to the 27th room, but—I mean, again, let Menestheus pick.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “But, look, I don't actually know where we're going. This is as far as I've ever gotten in the house. We came in, and I met up with the rest of the crew, and they were already on the way out. I know where we are, but I don't know—I mean, I know where we are in space.”

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: What's that big machine over there?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “I…” He gives an elaborate shrug.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Do you want to sit here in this room and read your books, and hope that this is your life for the rest of your life—sitting in this room, reading your books over and over again, and maybe or maybe not experiencing hunger? I'm not really sure how that goes. Or do you want to explore?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “I do want to stay with you. I—this, this is—yeah, right? Do you want to stay here by yourself? No! This is terrible! What happened here? Why is everything destroyed?”

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Yeah, I wouldn't want to stay here by myself. That would be scary and weird.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “Yeah, this guy gets it.”

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: This is just sort of Edric's thoughts -- this looks like a problem. “I'm not sure how to solve this problem. Maybe one of the wiser heads knows what to do.” He kind of looks around desperately at the rest of the party.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I mean, there's no—well, while they're talking, Txarro's just kind of looking around a little bit. I mean, there's—what, two doors out of this room?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Two doors: a door to the left, a door to the right, and stairs that—

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Right. And doors are not…

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You two—looking around is fine. I'll give you details. If you want more, you can do Investigation or Perception.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: The doors—do they just open? Are they locked?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, the doors on either side—and, in fact, when you come over to the stairs and look, there's a door at the top and a door at the bottom, also, maybe half a story away—open to a narrow corridor that's about ten feet long, with another door at the far end of it.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Like, both doors open to the same location?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: All four doors, yep.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Presumably we check all four doors, and they all look the same until you open them? So it's not that one opens to a delicious-smelling sort of kitchen and another opens to a discotheque room? They're all just tunnels?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: And there's no markings or footprints or…

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Excuse me, thank you. Yes, there is a little sign. You open the door and go into the hall. The door at the far end of the hall is locked, so you can't open it, and there is a little sign next to it that says, “All members of your group must come through together.” Then there is a number, like a little room-number marker, on the center of the door. So the door to the left is 12, to the right is 16, four is up, and 22 is down.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Wait, do these numbers have anything to do with the whole numbers-as-code thing with the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Menestheus does not seem to think so.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Mmm.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Well, he's a mathematician, I trust him.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “Yeah, I never really did interiors,” he says.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Oh, four, 12, 21, 17, or something? What'd you say?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: 12, 16, 4, 22. Yeah, you cannot discern any meaning to those numbers. Sorry.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Right. Twenty-two is down, 12 is left, four is right—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: For us.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: —four—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And 16 is right.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: 22 is closest to 27. Let's go that way.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Yeah, that's what I was thinking, too. I want to look at this machine first, though. I'm curious about it. What should I roll?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Why don't you do investigation?

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Oh, that's an eight total.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's big.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I mean, it's…

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's impressive-looking. It's not just decoration. When you put your hand on it, you can feel the hum of something, and maybe even a little static electricity or a little smell of ozone, but you can't make heads or tails of what it is.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: That's weird. Yeah, let's go to 22. That was downstairs?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Twenty-two. Awesome. You go down the stairs to 22, into the little corridor. The door at the far end is locked until all of you are in the space. You close the door behind you, and then the door on the other side becomes unlocked, and you can all go through it. You come through that door after this little corridor and down the stairs, through the continuation of the stairway that comes down through the center of this room. This room is about the same dimensions as the one you were in before, maybe 30 by 30 by 30 feet, and it has exits. If you're facing the same way you were in the room above, there's an entrance and exit in front of you and on either side, to your left and right. So you can go back up, or you can go left or right. This room is clearly a chapel. Actually, I need a little bit of help here, Tim. What would a Drankorian chapel—what gods would be in it?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Mos Numena. Let's—so—

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Same gods.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Yeah, same as Sembara.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, it's not different in kind from the chapels you've been in before, and there are spaces for the various gods, but the design and feel of it are really different. It's clearly older. It's like going—I don't know—into the Vatican or something: all this smooth, polished marble with little variegated flecks of color in it, in a way that nobody would build a chapel today, even though it's extremely impressive. Looking around the space, there's not much in the way of stuff in it. There are icons or statues, maybe art devoted to Mos Numena, but it's just the devotional space. There's not much else to it.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Are there numbers on the exits from here?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, I mean.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: This is a Drankorian chapel, and the Drankorian style was little alcoves for all the gods, right, Tim?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Yes, although…

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Probably.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Right. Although, conceivably, you might—right. Yes, you would typically have eight alcoves in a—

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I mean, is this intact, with holy symbols? Does it—does—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Y'all can, y'all can investigate.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I mean, forget even investigating. I'm just looking around. Is the Night Queen's altar recognizably the Night Queen's altar?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, although again, I'm sort of deferring to Tim because I don't know enough about Drankorian theology.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: So, if it's not been intentionally ruined, you would expect an architectural design that has eight separate alcoves, physically separated from each other in some way. Depending on how fancy it is, either elaborate, massive stained glass and jewel-gemmed carving-and-statuary things, or as simple as a plain, curvy wall or whatever. But the idea is that you architecturally isolate the eight altars to the Eight Divines, because there is a belief that the gods cannot hear you unless you are speaking to them alone. You don't want your prayer to the Night Queen—you want only the Night Queen to hear the prayer to the Night Queen. So, if it is intact, you would expect to see eight separate altars, with all eight of the Mos Numena—Eight Divines—represented with the same iconography as is common in modern Sembara. There are stylistic differences in the icons and things, but it would be clearly recognizable, especially to somebody like Edric.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: That said, of course, it could be built intentionally differently, or partially ruined, in which case some of those alcove and altar spaces might not be present. But that would be the assumed standard design.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, and that is indeed the design, with one exception. Nothing has been destroyed or defaced in any of the spaces for those gods, but, in order to get to the back exit of the room, you have to go around this little corridor that passes one of the enclosed spaces for the gods. On its back side, where there's just a blank wall heading out that back exit, it's like someone has taken a hammer or pickaxe to the blank wall and made a—divot? A void? A niche, maybe? It's about a foot or two across and a few feet high, just sort of smashed out from within it. The longer you spend looking at this, the stranger it seems. It's clearly intentional; it's not age, or something gone wrong with the masonry. Someone has smashed this thing out, and it's just an empty niche. Disturbing in a way that's difficult to articulate.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Well, before even worrying about the disturbing thing, Edric is gonna offer a prayer at the Night Queen's altar, take a few minutes over it, and try to get a sense of whether this is still consecrated. Is this actually still holy and working? Or is this dead—you know what I mean? Is it a live holy space, or is it dead?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, it definitely is. Inside that space—and presumably the others—yep. It's lovely. It's grounding. It sets you at ease a little bit.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Edric will kind of say over his shoulder, “I'm gonna just stay here for a minute, because it's very—but maybe someone should go see why that creepy thing is so creepy,” pointing at the hole. “That seems unnerving.”

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Tarek sticks his hand in the hole.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Good job, Tarek.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Give me a—what's a good save? How about a Wisdom save?

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Gold coins I wish to receive. Oh, a Wisdom save. Okay. That's also an eight in total.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You snatch it right back out again and feel, just for a second, like you're gonna vomit. But it passes.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's weird. You're not even conscious of pulling your hand back.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Beautiful.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Try this. Can you try that?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I feel like that's kind of a “you.”

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: No, man. It feels great. You should try it. What?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Yeah, this is definitely it.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Wait, wait, wait, why are we sticking our hand into creepy holes?

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: It's curiosity's sake.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I didn't mean do something dumb! Be safe!

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: You've not been around us very long.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I mean, I mean.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Oh, definitely.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Fair! I mean, I guess that—I'm sorry, that was not the appropriate word here. It's all good.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Maybe we should be a little less reckless in this place of uncertainty and oddness.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Have there been any signs of any other—I was asking about tracks and signs of passage before. Is there any indication that anybody else has been in this house anytime recently?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. In this room, you can't hear the humming of the machines that were in the entryway. You don't hear footsteps or voices. In fact, when you all slow down, it is perfectly silent.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Are there any souvenirs?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you could steal from one of the shrines to the gods?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No, don't do that.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: No, no you can't.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I consider it carefully, weighing costs and benefits.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I only see benefits.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: So in the entryway, it got all wrecked. Like, everything got all wrecked.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Mmm.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Here, people have been respectful of the religious sanctity. But in the non-sanctified space, somebody took out some sort of aggression, or panic, or—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, I think that's the right way to read the entryway: aggression or panic. It wasn't systematic; it wasn't the way it looks when a room's been tossed searching for something. It was like a flailing, almost. But not here.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: But by the divot.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, sorry—about the divot? No, intentional. It looks carved. Someone made it.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: What's the height above the floor of the divot?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: It doesn't look hacked? It looks nice? Well done?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It looks intentional. There's something about it that just feels mildly disgusting to look at, which your thinking mind does not make sense of, because it is just a little niche that someone took a hammer and chisel—or who even knows—and carved out of the back of a wall. But there's something uncomfortable about it.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Nauseating or, like, scary?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Both.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Yes, that's, yeah.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: All right. Good to know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Four exits, left, right, forward, up.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: So, I was asking before, are any of them numbered? Wait, up is back the way we came.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do you want to check the numbers on all the doors?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Yeah, yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, left is 25. Forward is 23. Right is 19.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Wait, what does “forward” mean in this circumstance?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: We're gonna assume that you were facing north when you entered this building?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Sixth quarter.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So the door went from south to north: you step north to enter it. So forward is north. We'll do it that way instead: north, west, east, and up.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Okay, so… West is 25.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep. North is 23.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: So north is… 23.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: East is 19. And up is 17.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Wait a minute.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Can we just check that up takes us back to the room we started in?

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Abacus.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So you all climb the flight of stairs. You step into the corridor, close the door behind you, and open the door in front of you. And you are standing—

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Oh, boy.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Not in the room that you came in.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You're standing instead in a room where almost the entire space is filled with massive mechanical equipment: huge tanks that feed through enormous pipes and go into the north wall. There are almost catwalks. The only available space to move is in these narrow little corridors that dodge through the immensity of all the equipment around you.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Is this plausibly the same room as the other one we were in, but back in time? Do we see the occupancy sign on the wall?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. The room that you came in through just had pipes and machinery against the far wall, the north wall. Here, almost the entire space is filled with machinery—arcane machinery. If you want to walk around, I can give you the exits and all of that, too.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: You know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So you can go up, down, west, or east. Oddly, against the north wall—you duck under a pipe and come out against the far wall—there's not an exit, but there is something that's almost like a window: a two-foot-by-two-foot cutout in the wall. You're looking through about, I don't know, three feet of stone wall, and on the other side of it, flush against it as if it's just a recessed back—but you get this distinct impression of it being a window—is a two-foot square of elaborately inscribed iron wall, just covered in runes and arcane markings that you can't decipher. Right next to it, after you've dodged under this big pipe to come out next to the window thing, there is a chair and a writing desk with a journal on top.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Let's have a look at that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They seem to be notes, arranged by date—dates that don't exactly make sense, or at least are a little challenging to translate from Drankorian in your head. There are probably about 30 pages filled in a small, maybe four-inch-by-six-inch notebook, comprising 15 or 20 entries. Some dates are really close together, and some are farther apart. There's no discernible pattern. The last one was a very long time ago now—I mean, 700-some years ago. It seems to be a transcription of a monologue, and it goes something like this. It's in quotes, and it says—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “When I get here, I do not know anyone. But there is a teacher who is very patient with me. He's teaching me about words. He's teaching me that words have an order. Words have a before and an after. He says that words are a game to play, because of course there is no such thing as before, and no such thing as after, except that words make it so. He says that, if I am to play games with the dreamers, I am learning about the order of words.” That's the first entry, and someone has scrawled notes to themselves below it, saying, “Child? Timeline?” The next entry continues with another quote: “I am learning about the order of words. My teacher teaches me about eating and drinking. About sunset and stars. About beginnings and endings.”

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: “He teaches me about the danger of cold iron and the fearfulness of the dreamers. He teaches me that words are letters, and brings me books, and I am reading them. He teaches me about trees, and roots, and leaves, and mushrooms, and houses, and hedges, and roads, and doors.” There's a note below it that says, “This list continues in this vein for some time.” The next entry is a little while later. It says, “This world is strange and scary. I am alone without the teacher. His evening is beginning, he tells me. He comes back, he tells me. He is not coming back. He is forgetting me. I'm not going to him. I'm going past his house. I'm going on and on and on and on.” There's another note below that says, “This continues for some time.” The entries go on in this vein, page after page: this odd jumble of things being learned—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —a sense of abandonment and fear, an almost childish pride in not needing a teacher anymore. Though, oddly, it's all written in the present tense. Finally, the last entry says: “I am grown. The world is very big. I'm tall. I stretch out. My hands are under a very bright and changing sky. My legs are reaching between trees and roots and leaves and mushrooms and becoming houses.” And that's the last entry in that.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: No commentary from the transcriber.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Transcriber has written 3 question marks below this.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Book is not fastened down in any way.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, no, it's just loose on top of it, yeah.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I'll look over it. Alright.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Wait, but is there, like—because there's the original writing—does the handwriting change at all over time?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: True that.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Little-kid handwriting, and then it gets—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, this is so good. What's happening is that this is a transcription, and there's a title page or a record of the—

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —date, then the name of the person doing the transcribing, then something to the effect of, “I heard the following,” and then that. There are a few different people doing the transcribing, taking shifts or rotating. But the speaker is not the one writing it down. This is something that's been heard.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I'll just flip to the 27th page and see if there's anything particularly interesting there.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's nothing that distinguishes it from the other pages. “The world is strange and scary, and I am alone. My teacher's party is beginning, and he will come, and he is coming back. He says he is not coming back. He is forgetting me over and over. I'm not going to him. I'm going on.”

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: So the teacher is Lord Endless—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Presumably.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: —Endless Ending. And then the student is the person in this house who we have not met yet.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I think the student becomes a whole bunch of houses.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Eric, did you freeze?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Yes, yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: At the most suspenseful possible point in the sentence.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: It was a great theory. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Eric?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Oh, becoming houses.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Oh, interesting. It's a creature that becomes houses.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: That's so weird.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I'll pick up the journal. I'll hand it to Tarek.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Mmhm.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I'm not sure that's it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, we heard you for just a second, Eric. Looking through the journal, I think maybe another way to say it is that it's almost like this is a—oh, no. Yeah, okay. No, you're all just very still. It's almost like this is a person who's perseverating. They keep coming back to the same things over and over again. Even though, when you read those sentences, you have a sense of a progression in time—this idea of a child, and then the child has grown—it's all written in the present tense. The speaker doesn't have that same kind of sensibility. There's not a narrative quality to it. It's just a whole lot of thoughts and statements.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: And there's a desk here that faces the weird runic-window thing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep, exactly. A desk and a chair.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: So possibly, if this desk is manned—if someone is at this desk for certain amounts of time—they sometimes hear this thing and transcribe it, and make a little note and reflection.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Oh, wait. You said that it's all different handwriting, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, like different people are transcribing.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: We should do the transcribing. How do we do it?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: You wanna just sit here and wait until you hear the voice of somebody that turns into a house, and—

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I want it, I want it. Who is it?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Tell me what you're doing, Kaito.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I wanna interview the person getting turned into a house.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: But are you gonna sit down in the chair?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Yeah, sit down on the chair.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You're sitting in the chair. Nothing's happening immediately.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: From the other pages, does it all start in any consistent way, or is it just like somebody starts talking?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, it's just that someone starts talking, and it starts in the middle. There's no instruction, like an invocation to say or something.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: A date or something like that? Is there anything, or does it just start? You know what I mean.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Wait, wait, say that one more time.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
